newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Union threatens to block BHP exports.
newsitem.headline: Union threatens to block BHP exports.

text.p: The Australian Workers Union said on Monday it would consider launching a coordinated union campaign to block the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's exports if BHP shuts down most of its Newcastle Steel operations.
"I wouldn't rule out industrial action and the industrial action could be Australia-wide," the Australian Workers Union's (AWU) Newcastle Secretary Maurie Rudd told Reuters.

"We're also looking at other unions being involved in stopping BHP's exports," Rudd said, adding the Maritime Unions and other AWU unions at BHP's Western Australian iron ore operations could get involved in coordinated ACTU campaign.
Rudd said BHP was expected to announce the results of its steel review on Tuesday in Newcastle.
He said BHP was likely to shut down the bulk of its steel making operations.
The AWU planned to hold a delegates meeting in Newcastle on Tuesday and a mass stop-work meeting on Friday, he said.

Newspapers reported earlier on Monday that Newcastle's two aging blast furnaces and coke ovens were likely to be closed by 2000, leaving only the rod, bar and wire mills which employ about 900 workers.
The shutdowns would leave about 3,000 workers out of work.
A spokesman for BHP Steel was not immediately available for comment.
Newspapers and Rudd also said there was speculation BHP planned to eventually shut down all its Australian steel operations.
BHP's shares were two cents lower at A$17.44 at 10.45 a.m. (0045 GMT) on Monday.
